messages:
maria: CI `publish-image` is failing on push to registry.redwood.internal — Docker push returns 401 for manifest upload. This started after I changed the Dockerfile stages (tiny tweak). Anyone seen similar?

deploy-bot: [ci] publish-image failed — https://ci.redwood.internal/builds/9823 (logs attached)

kevin: can you paste the exact error snippet from the push logs? 401 usually creds but could be token scope.

maria: gist of push logs: `denied: requested access to the resource is denied` then `http status 401` during `PUT /v2/engine/manifests/latest`

maria: fwiw I rotated a service-account secret this morning (for another PR) but I updated the k8s secret in the infra namespace. not sure if registry robot got impacted.

tomas: we rotated the deploy robot key yesterday night as part of infra cleanup. should still be valid though. olivia, any registry logs?

olivia: seeing a few auth failures around that timestamp from the registry: `token verification failed: token not found` for client `ci-runner-4`. Also intermittent `object storage checksum mismatch` on blob PUTs — looks like registry is sometimes failing to persist blobs to s3 gateway and returns inconsistent state.

kevin: hmm two separate things — token not found (auth) and checksum mismatch (storage). could be transient; did the CI runner reuse a cached layer from a different build using inline cache? that can trigger weird manifest conflicts if blobs differ.

maria: CI uses kaniko with inline cache enabled in our pipeline. maybe the Dockerfile change invalidated some cache layers. want me to force a no-cache run?

tomas: yes please try a rerun with no cache: set `KANIKO_CACHE=true`->no, or run kaniko with `--no-push` then `--no-cache`? For buildkit: `--no-cache` and `BUILDKIT_INLINE_CACHE=0`. Also ensure the runner picks up latest registry credentials.

maria: rerunning with `--no-cache` and fresh creds now, will post logs.

(maria later): rerun completed: build succeeded locally but `docker push` hit `500 write timeout` during blob upload (second layer).

olivia: that `500 write timeout` matches S3 gateway timeouts I saw — one of the storage nodes reported high latency and returned `416`/`checksum mismatch` earlier. looks like object storage flapping.

kevin: ok so both auth and storage flakiness. For short term workaround: can we switch CI to fallback registry `registry-fallback.redwood.internal` (read-replica) or upload artifacts to GCR? Also we should avoid reusing inline cache across runners until storage healthy.

tomas: I'll restart the registry deployment in prod-ns and invalidate its cache (Harbor GC not needed, just restart the registry pod to clear stuck uploads). Olivia — can you check S3 node health and raise a PagerDuty if it's not healthy?

olivia: looking at s3-gateway-2, it's showing elevated 95th latency and some corrupted multipart uploads. I triggered a rotation of the gateway and cleared dangling multipart uploads for the last 2 hours. If that doesn't help I'll escalate.

(maria later): after registry pod restart + s3 gateway rotation, I re-queued the build to use `--no-cache` and it pushed fine. all green now :tada:

kevin: awesome. follow-ups: 1) audit whether CI runners are reusing inline caches cross-runner (seems risky with flaky storage), 2) alerting: add a combined alarm on registry blob PUT error rate + s3-gateway latency so we can detect this earlier.

tomas: added a TODO to infra backlog for safer cache invalidation and a runbook for registry restart + S3 multipart cleanup.

maria: thanks all — leaving the original PR open but the image publish part is fixed. will re-enable inline cache after we confirm storage stability.

olivia: noted — I'll keep an eye on s3-gateway for next 24h and post if any new anomalies show up.
